item.title: The Last Dance: Did Distractions Weigh on the Last Sundance Sales Market in Park City?
item.description: Between nostalgia for Park City, mourning the loss of Robert Redford, and the grim news of the Minneapolis shooting, people had things on their minds other than movies.

item.title: The ’Texas Chainsaw Massacre’ Is Coming Back to Life — Thanks to A24, JT Mollner, and Glen Powell
item.description: The horror franchise will first get a television series, with plans for a new film — and seemingly much more — also in the works.

item.title: ‘Fallout’ Season 2 Finale Ghoulishly Chases Our Attention, When It Could Be Winning Our Hearts
item.description: After a season focused on plot extensions and world-building, Episode 8, “The Strip,” succumbs to a troubling Hollywood trend: It’s easy to watch, and easier to forget.

item.title: ‘Tow’ Trailer: Oscar Nominee Rose Byrne Goes Blonde for Heart-Tugging, Fact-Based Dramedy
item.description: Directed by Stephanie Laing, the true story of a woman living in her Toyota Camry will be Byrne's next release after her recent Oscar nomination.

item.title: The Best Director Oscar Race May Be a Lot More Competitive Than We Think
item.description: The DGA Awards will clear up who the Best Director frontrunner is, but there is a path for every Oscar nominee to win.

item.title: SXSW 2026 Announces More Film and TV, Led by ‘The Comeback’ Season 3
item.description: The new selections join previously announced headliners "I Love Boosters," "Margo's Got Money Troubles," and more.

item.title: ‘A Poet’ Is a Movie About Artistic Frustration. For Its Director, It’s Also About the Experience of Making Indie Features
item.description: Simón Mesa Soto, who also teaches in his home country, directs the Cannes winner about a curmudgeonly, glory-less poet; it mirrors local filmmakers' own issues with trying to appease funders and appeal to a very limited audience.

item.title: Kristen Stewart Is Restoring a 1925 Movie Theater in LA’s Highland Park
item.description: The actress and director announced plans to reopen Los Angeles' Highland Theatre, which closed in 2024.

item.title: Jonathan Demme’s ‘Married to the Mob’ Arrives on 4K: Why His Pre-‘Silence of the Lambs’ Crime Comedy Is a Must-See
item.description: Cinématographe's 4K debut of the 1988 crime comedy, starring Michelle Pfeiffer and Matthew Modine, offers a new opportunity to examine Demme's transitional film between "Something Wild" and "The Silence of the Lambs."

item.title: Madelaine Petsch Stands by ‘The Strangers’ Spinoff Needing Three Films to Feel Complete
item.description: The actress and producer looked back on her experience releasing the slasher series with IndieWire.
